body:
## Problem

Issue #1089 reports that the contrast linter can suggest `bind fills/0` for a text finding after a button fill changes. That path belongs to the parent backdrop, not the text node, and applying the suggested binding can make contrast worse.

## Reproduction

A text label with `#F4F4F5` on a button bound to `var:Color/Danger` produces a contrast finding. On the affected path, the old suggestion selected a parent backdrop variable and attached it to the text finding as `fills/0`.

Expected: a suggestion targets a valid property on the failing text node and improves contrast, or no suggestion is returned.

## Root cause

`Suggest_passing_variable` generated both foreground and parent-backdrop candidates, but `FixSuggestion` has no target-node field. The parent property was therefore serialized as if it belonged to the text node.

## Fix

Remove parent-backdrop candidates from text findings. Keep foreground variable suggestions, which target the failing text node's existing fill property and retain the current scoring behavior.

## Validation

- Regression was red on the base: the affected fixture observed an invalid parent `fills/0` suggestion (exit 101; evidence in mission logs).
- `cargo test -p designos-render --test lint_contrast --locked` — 11 passed.
- `cargo test -p designos-doc --lib lint::rules --locked` — 18 passed.
- `cargo test --workspace --locked` with external Playwright 1.64.1/Chromium harness — pass; all workspace suites and web capture 8/8 passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` — pass.
- `cargo test -p designos-gpu --locked` — pass.
- `cargo test -p designos-mcp --locked` — pass.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` — pass.
- Independent review of exact product diff — PASS, no severity findings.

## Scope and limitation

This patch suppresses backdrop-only suggestions because the current suggestion contract cannot identify a separate parent target. Valid foreground suggestions remain available. UI rendering was not changed.

Refs #1089
